title: Trifork's open-source contributions already land inside Danish public-health infrastructure
content:
Trifork contributes to an open-source framework used in MedCom infrastructure modernisation and in FUT, the Danish telemedicine programme. That is the fact the research weighs most heavily: the firm's open-source work already reaches Danish public-health infrastructure, which is simultaneously the target vertical and the target licence model.

Existing contribution changes the nature of the ask. The firm does not have to be convinced that openly licensed components belong in public healthcare, because it already puts them there, and the institutional relationships that make such contributions possible are in place. What remains is a technical argument about what the framework does not record, rather than a positioning argument about open source in the public sector.

The second asset is distribution. Trifork runs the GOTO conferences, with more than 38 million YouTube views recorded in the workbook — a developer audience that cannot be bought at any price. The research's summary is that this is the best combined profile found: the right vertical, the right licence model, and a channel to developers attached to the same firm.
